paper_metadata.title: Composition and microstructure design for an ultra-high strength and high-temperature dual-phase Ti alloy using cluster formula approach

evidence.quote: Dual-phase Ti alloys are known for good processabilities but their mechanical strengths are not sufficient both at room and at high temperatures.

A high-temperature and high-strength dual-phase titanium alloy Ti-6Al-14Zr-2V-2Mo-1Nb (wt%) is designed based on the composition of the widely used dual-phase Ti-6Al-4V, with additional (Zr, Mo, Nb) co-alloying.

samples.material_state: solution-treated at 840 °C and aged at 550 °C for 4 h

evidence.quote: A high-temperature and high-strength dual-phase titanium alloy Ti-6Al-14Zr-2V-2Mo-1Nb (wt%) is designed based on the composition of the widely used dual-phase Ti-6Al-4V, with additional (Zr, Mo, Nb) co-alloying.
surpassing the best 500 °C dual-phase titanium alloy, TC21 (Ti-6Al-3Mo-2Sn-2Zr-2Nb-1.5Cr-0.1Si) by more than 30 %.

process_steps.input_state: elemental metals Ti, Al, V, Mo, Nb, Zr (purity > 99.9%)

evidence.quote: alloy ingots weighting 80 g, with a diameter of approximately 45 mm and 14.5 mm in height, are prepared in a vacuum arc-melting furnace under an argon atmosphere.
The ingots are initially held at 900°C for 0.5 h, and then subjected to multiple passes of hot rolling

parameters.deformation: total deformation rate of about 80%, thickness 2.5 mm

evidence.quote: then subjected to multiple passes of hot rolling to obtain plates with a thickness of 2.5 mm and a total deformation rate of about 80 %.
The rolled plates are solution-treated for 1 h in dual-phase zone below Tβ, at 760, 800, 840, and 880 °C under vacuum and are air-cooled.
Finaly, aging is performed in vacuum at 550 °C for 4 h, followed by air cooling to room temperature.
The rolled plates are solution-treated for 1 h in dual-phase zone below Tβ, at 760, 800, 840, and 880 °C under vacuum and are air-cooled.
Finaly, aging is performed in vacuum at 550 °C for 4 h, followed by air cooling to room temperature.
The rolled plates are solution-treated for 1 h in dual-phase zone below Tβ, at 760, 800, 840, and 880 °C under vacuum and are air-cooled.
Finaly, aging is performed in vacuum at 550 °C for 4 h, followed by air cooling to room temperature.
The rolled plates are solution-treated for 1 h in dual-phase zone below Tβ, at 760, 800, 840, and 880 °C under vacuum and are air-cooled.
Finaly, aging is performed in vacuum at 550 °C for 4 h, followed by air cooling to room temperature.

Solutioning at 840 °C represents the best compromise, achieving the maximized αp volume fraction (~30 vol%) before agglomeration, while maintaining sufficiently fine αs, which optimizes both strength and plasticity.
the present 550 °C/4 h aging basically meets the compositional design expectation.

The 840 °C solution-plus-aging specimen is further characterized for microstructure and composition, and the results are shown in Fig. 8, where the α phase distribution image (b) clearly shows the equiaxed αp grains (red) embedded in the βt matrix (blue).

at the lower solution temperatures of 760 °C and 800 °C, some of the αp grains undergoes significant agglomeration, i.e., multiple αp grains are merged into one irregularly elongated grain, and at the lowest solution temperature of 760 °C, the agglomeration even forms a chain-like structure.
